answer: The second-order proximity between two vertices u and v becomes 0 when they have no shared neighbors, i.e., they share no common links. In terms of their neighbor sets, this is stated as N(u) ∩ N(v) = ∅ (the intersection of their neighborhoods is empty). Second-order proximity depends on how similarly the two vertices' neighborhoods are connected, so with no shared neighbors it is 0.
